belief: If I give more, God must give me more.
meta: A Christian look at the false belief that if you give more God must give you more, with Scripture, questions, and homework for replacing it with the truth.
origins: Preaching that promises financial return for giving (“sow a seed to get a harvest”). Financial stress that makes a quick answer appealing. Giving with the hope of getting out of debt. Disappointment when giving did not lead to more money. Treating God like an investment that must pay off.
teaches: God loves a cheerful giver, and generosity is a beautiful part of following Christ. But Scripture calls us to give freely, not as a way to obligate God. Jesus praised the widow who gave all she had, not because of what she would receive, but because of her heart. We are told to store up treasure in heaven and to be content with what we have. God does provide for His children, but He is not a vending machine.
self_statements: If I give enough, God has to bless me financially.
My giving is an investment with God.
If I’m still struggling, I didn’t give enough.
God owes me for what I’ve given.
The more I give, the richer I should get.
I give so that I’ll get.
errors: Treating God like a business partner who owes a return.
Believing giving controls what God must do.
Blaming financial struggles on not giving enough.
Giving in order to get, rather than out of love.
questions: Why does God love a cheerful giver?
What did the widow receive in return for her gift?
Am I giving to love God and others, or to get something?
Can God be obligated by anything I do?
Where does Jesus tell me to store up treasure?
Have I made money the measure of God’s blessing?
What would giving look like if I expected nothing back?
truth: I do not give to make God give me more. I give because God has been generous to me, and because I love Him and others. God loves a cheerful giver, and He provides for my needs, but He is not obligated by my gifts. My treasure is in heaven, and I can learn to be content.
hw_questions: Why does God love a cheerful giver?
What did the widow get in return?
Am I giving to love or to get?
Where does Jesus tell me to store treasure?
What if I gave expecting nothing back?
hw_truths: I give because God has been generous to me.
God is not obligated by my gifts.
My true treasure is in heaven.
Godliness with contentment is great gain.
I can give freely and trust God to provide.
log: Each day, write one way I was generous with time, money, or kindness, and what I received that wasn’t money.
name_example: Sarah should give what she has decided in her heart to give, not out of regret or compulsion. For God loves a cheerful giver.
actions: Give one small gift this week in secret,
expecting nothing in return, and notice how it feels.
Write down every way God has provided for you
in the past year that did not come as more money.
and write what Jesus says about money and trust.
Talk with a wise Christian or financial counselor
about a healthy plan for giving and saving.
prayer: Father, thank You for Your generosity to me. Help me reject the lie that if I give more, You must give me more. Make me a cheerful giver who gives out of love, not to get. Teach me contentment, and help me store up treasure in heaven. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
